ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity dark field with high-intensity white pixels localized at the distal tips and isolated spots, creating a low global contrast ratio of approximately 1:20.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant dark grey/black field. High-contrast white contiguous blobs localized at the distal tips of both lobes. A single high-contrast circular white spot located on the mid-ventral surface of the left lobe. A series of parallel vertical white linear segments on the distal region of the right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Central V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 48 degrees and a vertical depth accounting for roughly 15% of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Low-frequency, low-amplitude serrations along the primary trailing edge boundary. High-amplitude irregular topographic variance and jagged edges localized at the extreme distal tips.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetrical convex curvature along the lower boundary, transitioning into a mild concavity at the distal sweep of both lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Highly localized circular white pixel cluster on the mid-left lobe. Dense, textured, high-contrast white and ochre clusters at the terminal ends of both lobes indicating barnacle colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Series of 6-8 vertically oriented, unaligned linear white pixel disruptions on the distal portion of the right lobe, consistent with rake marks.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive white scarring and irregular material buildup on the distal tips of both lobes; distinct circular depigmentation scar on the left lobe; vertical linear rake marks on the right lobe distal surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Visible trajectory of high-intensity white pixels representing water droplets shedding from the leftmost tip of the fluke.
